name: Hudson Bay Lowland

geo.extent: Southern and western shores of Hudson Bay and James Bay

description: The main central depression on the surface of the Canadian Shield: a low, swampy plain with subdued glacial features and a belt of raised beaches bordering Hudson Bay. One of the largest wetland landscapes in North America, almost roadless.

attributes.ecozone_named_in_source: Hudson Plains (plains; wetlands, some herb-moss-lichen tundra, evergreen forest; cold to mild, semi-arid; discontinuous permafrost)
attributes.protected_area_example: Wapusk National Park (MB): spans boreal forest to arctic tundra; one of the world's largest polar bear maternity denning areas

sources.title: The Atlas of Canada – Physiographic Regions of Canada (map 1254A compiled by H.S. Bostock, 1967, with descriptive text)

limitations: Physiographic description summarised from the Atlas of Canada; the map dates from 1967 (Bostock) and boundaries are generalised at 1:5 million. Lat/lon not given because the record describes an extensive region, not a point. Wetland superlative and roadless note are agent-04 interpretation.
